The elections will coincide with [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives and various [[2026 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2026 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. The primary elections took place on June 23, 2026.{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|website= NCSL |access-date=5 August 2025}} {{Horizontal TOC|nonum=yes|limit=2}} == Failed redistricting attempt == In November 2025, as a part of the broader [[2025–2026 United States redistricting]], Governor [[Wes Moore]] announced the formation of the Governor's Redistricting Advisory Commission, which was tasked with holding public hearings and providing recommendations for a new congressional map.{{cite news |last1=Sears |first1=Bryan P. |title=Moore forges ahead with redistricting effort, announcing advisory commission |url=https://marylandmatters.org/2025/11/04/moore-forges-ahead-with-redistricting-effort-announcing-advisory-commission/ |access-date=November 4, 2025 |work=Maryland Matters |date=November 4, 2025}} On January 20, 2026, the commission voted to recommend a congressional map that would redraw [[Maryland's 1st congressional district]] to improve the Democratic Party's chances of winning it.{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Pamela |title=Maryland commission recommends new congressional boundaries favoring Democrats |url=https://www.thebanner.com/politics-power/state-government/maryland-congressional-redistricting-vote-CFYGKDSGN5CD7NTAUEDP4ZAXQ4/ |access-date=January 20, 2026 |work=[[The Baltimore Banner]] |date=January 20, 2026 |language=en}} The map passed the [[Maryland House of Delegates]] by a 99–37 vote on February 2, 2026,{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Pamela |title=Maryland House approves congressional map; expected to stall in Senate |url=https://www.thebanner.com/politics-power/state-government/maryland-house-redistricting-vote-JOAA2YPSCJE5DLTUQKDLSH3ZW4/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |work=[[The Baltimore Banner]] |date=February 2, 2026 |language=en}} but died in the [[Maryland Senate]] after Senate President [[Bill Ferguson (politician)|Bill Ferguson]] refused to hold a vote on the redistricting bill in the Senate.{{cite news |last1=Gaskill |first1=Hannah |title=Is MD's midcycle redistricting battle over? Yes, Ferguson says. |url=https://thedailyrecord.com/2026/02/20/maryland-opens-midcycle-redistricting-closed/ |access-date=February 20, 2026 |work=[[The Daily Record (Maryland)|The Daily Record]] |date=February 20, 2026}} In August 2026, the Maryland General Assembly convened for a special session, during which it passed [[2026 Maryland Question 3|Question 3]], which would exempt Maryland's congressional districts from guidelines in the [[Constitution of Maryland]] that require legislative districts to respect natural boundaries and the boundaries of political subdivisions. If approved by voters, it may allow Democrats to redraw its congressional maps ahead of the 2028 elections.{{cite news |last1=Gregory |first1=Matt |title=Maryland legislators approved a 'redistricting' referendum |url=https://www.wusa9.com/article/news/politics/maryland-house-sentae-approves-redistricting-ballot/65-59680979-7185-4501-8021-389586c1aa1b |access-date=September 12, 2026 |work=[[WUSA (TV)]] |date=September 12, 2026}} ==District 1== {{Infobox election | election_name = 2026 Maryland's 1st congressional district election | country = Maryland | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Maryland#District 1 | previous_year = 2024 | next_election = 2028 United States House of Representatives elections in Maryland #District 1 | next_year = 2028 | image_size = x150px | image1 = Andy Harris 115th Congress Higher dif (cropped).jpg | nominee1 = [[Andy Harris (politician)|Andy Harris]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = Dan Schwartz 2026-10-13.png | nominee2 = Dan Schwartz | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | map_image = | map_size = 200px | map_caption = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Andy Harris (politician)|Andy Harris]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{see also|Maryland's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district encompasses the entire [[Eastern Shore of Maryland]], including [[Salisbury, Maryland|Salisbury]], [[Harford County, Maryland|Harford County]], and parts of north [[Baltimore County, Maryland|Baltimore County]].
